newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar propels German shares to fresh record highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar propels German shares to fresh record highs.

text.p: Germany's blue chip DAX index ended bourse dealings at an all-time closing high on Wednesday, continuing a rally sparked late on Tuesday by the dollar's recovery against the mark.
"The lights are all on green," said one trader.
The 30-share DAX finished floor dealings up 39.13 points, or 1.43 percent, at a record close of 2,773.43 points, and just off an intraday high of 2,775.96 points reached in in late dealings.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computer trade in the DAX index, ended slightly below the bourse close at 2,770.61 points, up 6.31 points, having earlier touched an intraday record of 2,778.83 points.

Dealers said an overnight record close on Wall Street, strength on the DAX future contract and surprisingly good nine month results from utility giant Veba had all helped feed the rally, initially triggered by the dollar's recovery.
On Tuesday, the U.S. currency had been sitting at its lowest level for two months just above 1.49 marks, weighing particularly on Germany's export-oriented chemicals and carmaker shares.
But later on Tuesday comments by two Bundesbankers about the low level of the dollar, sent it up above the crucial 1.50 mark level, in turn encouraging German shares.
Although some dealers said the index was overbought from a technical point of view, they still predicted that the DAX would continue to soar.
"We could make 2,800 points by the end of the week," said one dealer, "The sentiment is great and everyone is bullish."
Dealers said the DAX was shaping up perfectly for the biggest flotation in its history next week when shares in national telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom will be traded for the first time.

Wednesday's best DAX performer was Veba, which surprised the market by reporting a 25 percent climb in nine month net profit to 1,227 billion marks. Veba ended IBIS dealings up over four percent, or 3.67 marks at 87.67 marks, having earlier reached an all-time high of 88.70 marks.
Meanwhile nine month figures released by chemicals and drugs group BASF AG were somewhat disappointing, dealers said, and the stock ended computer trade down 86 pfennigs at 51.61 marks.
Diversified industrial giant Daimler Benz AG reached an all-time high of 99.50 marks in IBIS trade, before paring gains to end the day up three marks at 99.10 marks.
Dealers said that as a major exporter Daimler had benefited in particular from the dollar recovery and said some investment houses had also repeated earlier buy recommendations on the stock.
